mainTopic: קידושין on conditions about the man himself, the ten portions of traits, and why unspoken intentions do not count
overview: The amud opens by explaining what a man must know when he betroths a woman on condition that he knows תורה, and the exact wording of his claim changes the standard. A ברייתא then goes through conditions a man might set about himself: a תלמיד, a חכם, a גבור, or an עשיר. For each one it sets a realistic minimum instead of demanding greatness. If he says he is a צדיק or a רשע, the קידושין can take effect even if he seems to be the opposite, because one thought can change a person in a moment. The גמרא then brings an אגדה about ten portions of each trait coming down to the world. It stops to work out why arrogance belongs to עילם and not to בבל. A new משנה rules that when a man betroths on a spoken condition about himself that turns out false, she is not betrothed. This holds even if she says she didn't care, and the same is true when she misled him. The גמרא then tells of a man who sold his property planning to move to ארץ ישראל. רבא rules that unspoken intentions do not count, and the search for רבא's source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does 'Torah' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of Torah knowledge the earlier opinion meant when it said a man claiming to be a שונה must know 'תורה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'Torah'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the word 'תורה' in the earlier discussion. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, a man betrothed a woman 'on condition that I am a שונה', and one opinion said that means he must know 'תורה'. The word is vague. It could mean simply reading the פסוקים, or something deeper, so the גמרא asks which.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (a standard opening for a clarifying question)
Torah: here, the kind of learning the man must know

phrases.english: What is 'Torah'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a clarification of a term from the preceding discussion (before this section).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What level of Torah knowledge does 'תורה' require for the condition to be fulfilled?

steps.title: It means the interpretation of the Torah
steps.stepSummary: 'Torah' here means מדרש תורה: knowing how the פסוקים are explained and expounded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means interpreting the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. 'Torah' means מדרש תורה, the explanations drawn out of the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This raises the bar above simply reading the text. To count as a שונה under this opinion, the man must know the Torah together with the teachings that come from studying it closely.

keyTerms.meaning: Explaining the Torah: drawing laws and lessons out of the פסוקים

phrases.english: The interpretation of the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Torah' means מדרש תורה, the expounding of the Torah.

steps.title: The exact words the man used change the standard
steps.stepSummary: Knowing מדרש תורה is enough only if he said 'I have learned'. If he said 'I am a תנא', he must know הלכות, ספרא, ספרי, and תוספתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only when he told her, 'I have learned.' But if he told her, 'I am a תנא,' it is not enough until he has learned הלכות, ספרא, ספרי, and תוספתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the rule it just gave. What counts depends on exactly how the man described himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I have learned' (תנינא) only says he has studied, so מדרש תורה is enough. 'I am a תנא' (תנא אנא) claims a title, so he must know the major collections of תורה שבעל פה. A stronger claim needs stronger proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only... (introduces a limit on a rule)
I am a תנא, a person who knows the teachings of the תנאים
Collections of מדרש on ויקרא (ספרא) and on במדבר and דברים (ספרי)
A collection of teachings of the תנאים that goes alongside the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in קידושין conditions, the exact wording a person uses decides what he has promised.

phrases.english: And this applies when he said to her, 'I have learned,'
phrases.notes: 'This' means the rule from step 2, that knowing מדרש תורה is enough.

phrases.english: but if he said to her, 'I am a תנא,'
it is not enough until he has learned הלכות,
ספרא, ספרי, and תוספתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 2 to one specific wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'תנינא' needs only מדרש תורה; 'תנא אנא' needs הלכות, ספרא, ספרי, and תוספתא.
steps.whatToRemember: The more the man claims about himself, the more he must actually know for the קידושין to take effect.

steps.title: 'I am a student': no need to be a great scholar
steps.stepSummary: A man who says 'I am a תלמיד' does not need to be like שמעון בן עזאי or שמעון בן זומא. He only needs to be able to answer one question on whatever he has studied, even in מסכת כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'on condition that I am a תלמיד', we do not require him to be like שמעון בן עזאי or שמעון בן זומא. Rather, it is anyone who can answer when asked one thing, anywhere in what he has learned, even in מסכת כלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of conditions with 'I am a תלמיד' and sets a low, realistic bar for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The famous students שמעון בן עזאי and שמעון בן זומא are not the measure. All he needs is to answer one question correctly on something he has learned. Even a small, lesser-studied מסכת such as מסכת כלה is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not say: the standard is not set that high
מסכת כלה, a short and less commonly studied מסכת

phrases.english: 'On condition that I am a student':
we do not say he must be like שמעון בן עזאי
and like שמעון בן זומא,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כֹּל שֶׁשּׁוֹאֲלִין אוֹתוֹ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
phrases.english: rather, anyone who, when asked anywhere
one thing in his learning, can say it,
even in מסכת כלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next condition in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'תלמיד' means anyone who can answer one question on what he has studied.

steps.title: 'I am a wise man': no need to be like the sages of יבנה
steps.stepSummary: A man who says 'I am a חכם' does not need to be like the sages of יבנה. He only needs to be able to answer a question of wisdom on any subject.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'on condition that I am a חכם', we do not require him to be like the sages of יבנה, like רבי עקיבא and his colleagues. Rather, it is anyone who can answer when asked a matter of wisdom on any subject.
steps.whatsHappening: Next condition: 'I am a חכם'. Again the ברייתא sets a reachable standard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חכם is one step above a תלמיד. He must be able to answer a matter of wisdom on any subject, not just in the one area he studied. But he still does not need to match רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: 'On condition that I am a wise man':
we do not say like the sages of יבנה,
like רבי עקיבא and his colleagues,
rather, anyone who, when asked
a matter of wisdom anywhere, can say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 4, applied to 'חכם'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'חכם' means anyone who can answer a question of wisdom on any subject.

steps.title: 'I am strong': no need to be a famous warrior
steps.stepSummary: A man who says 'I am a גבור' does not need to be like אבנר בן נר or יואב בן צרויה. It is enough that his friends fear him because of his strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'on condition that I am a גבור', we do not require him to be like אבנר בן נר or יואב בן צרויה. Rather, it is anyone whose friends are afraid of him because of his strength.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from Torah conditions to physical strength, using the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The standard is measured against the people around him, not against legendary army generals. If his own friends are afraid of his strength, that is enough.

phrases.english: 'On condition that I am a strong man':
we do not say like אבנר בן נר
and like יואב בן צרויה,
rather, anyone whose friends are afraid of him
because of his strength.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern, applied to physical strength.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'גבור' means anyone whose friends fear him because of his strength.

steps.title: 'I am rich': no need to be among the richest
steps.stepSummary: A man who says 'I am an עשיר' does not need wealth like רבי אלעזר בן חרסום or רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. It is enough that the people of his town honor him for his wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'on condition that I am an עשיר', we do not require him to be like רבי אלעזר בן חרסום or רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. Rather, it is anyone whom the people of his town honor because of his wealth.
steps.whatsHappening: Next condition: wealth. The same realistic, local standard applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again the measure is his own surroundings. If his own town treats him as a rich man, he counts as rich, even if he is nowhere near the famous wealthy sages.

phrases.english: 'On condition that I am a rich man':

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִים כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן חַרְסוֹם
phrases.english: we do not say like רבי אלעזר בן חרסום
and like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כֹּל שֶׁבְּנֵי עִירוֹ מְכַבְּדִים אוֹתוֹ
phrases.english: rather, anyone whom the people of his town honor
because of his wealth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern, applied to wealth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'עשיר' means anyone his townspeople honor for his wealth.
steps.whatToRemember: For תלמיד, חכם, גבור, and עשיר, the ברייתא never demands greatness. It asks only for a real, recognizable level, often measured by the people around him.

steps.title: 'I am righteous': even a wicked man may qualify
steps.stepSummary: If he says 'on condition that I am a צדיק', even a completely wicked man is מקודשת, because he may have thought of תשובה in his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'on condition that I am a צדיק', even if he is a complete רשע she is betrothed, because perhaps he thought of תשובה in his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The pattern changes here. Instead of setting a minimum standard, the ברייתא says that even someone who looks like the total opposite might fulfill the condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Righteousness depends on what is inside a person's heart, which no one else can see. A single thought of תשובה can turn him into a צדיק, so we cannot rule out that the condition was fulfilled.

phrases.english: 'On condition that I am a righteous man':
even if he is a completely wicked man, she is betrothed,
for perhaps he thought of repentance in his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list, but the rule now depends on hidden thoughts rather than a visible minimum standard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a complete רשע who says 'I am a צדיק' makes the קידושין take effect, since he may have done תשובה in his heart.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches how strong a single thought of תשובה is: it can change a person's status in an instant.

steps.title: 'I am wicked': even a righteous man may qualify
steps.stepSummary: If he says 'on condition that I am a רשע', even a completely righteous man is מקודשת, because he may have had a thought of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'on condition that I am a רשע', even if he is a complete צדיק she is betrothed, because perhaps he thought about עבודה זרה in his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the mirror image of the previous case. Even a man who looks completely righteous might really be a רשע inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thought can lift a person, and a thought can also bring him down. A thought of עבודה זרה is serious enough to make him a רשע, so here too we cannot rule out that the condition was fulfilled.

phrases.english: 'On condition that I am a wicked man':
even if he is a completely righteous man, she is betrothed,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא הִרְהֵר דְּבַר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּדַעְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: for perhaps he thought about idol worship in his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror-image case of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a complete צדיק who says 'I am a רשע' makes the קידושין take effect, since he may have had a thought of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatToRemember: With צדיק and רשע, we cannot see into a person's heart, and one thought can change his status in either direction. So the קידושין take effect even when he seems to be the opposite of what he claimed.

steps.title: Ten portions of each trait came down to the world
steps.stepSummary: Ten קבים each of wisdom, beauty, wealth, poverty and arrogance came down to the world. One place took nine of each: ארץ ישראל took wisdom, ירושלים took beauty, רומי took wealth, בבל took poverty, and עילם took arrogance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ten measures of wisdom came down to the world. ארץ ישראל took nine, and the whole rest of the world got one. Ten measures of beauty came down. ירושלים took nine, and the rest of the world got one. Ten measures of wealth came down. רומי took nine, and the rest of the world got one. Ten measures of poverty came down. בבל took nine, and the rest of the world got one. Ten measures of arrogance came down. עילם took nine, and the rest of the world got one.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא was just talking about traits like wisdom and wealth, it now brings a related teaching about how these traits were divided among different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every line follows the same pattern: ten portions come down, one place takes nine, and the whole rest of the world shares one. The last line, that arrogance went to עילם, is the line the גמרא will question in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Plural of קַב, a unit of measure; here it means 'portions'
עילם, a land east of בבל

phrases.english: Ten kav of wisdom came down to the world,
phrases.notes: A קב is a measure of volume. Here it just means 'ten portions' of the trait.

phrases.english: the Land of Israel took nine
and the whole rest of the world got one.
Ten kav of beauty came down to the world,
Jerusalem took nine
and the whole rest of the world got one.
Ten kav of wealth came down to the world,
Rome took nine
and the whole rest of the world got one.
Ten kav of poverty came down to the world,
Babylonia took nine
and the whole rest of the world got one.
Ten kav of arrogance came down to the world,
Eilam took nine
and the whole rest of the world got one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching about traits, connected to the earlier discussion of a חכם and an עשיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of five traits came down in ten portions, and one place took nine. Arrogance went to עילם, and poverty went to בבל.

steps.title: A פסוק suggests arrogance went to בבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that arrogance went to עילם. A פסוק in זכריה describes a measure being carried to the land of שנער (בבל), and רבי יוחנן explains that this is flattery and arrogance going down to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did arrogance not go down to בבל? But it is written: 'I lifted my eyes and saw two women coming out, with wind in their wings. They had wings like a stork's wings, and they lifted the measure between earth and heaven. I said to the angel who spoke with me: Where are they taking the measure? He said to me: To build her a house in the land of שנער.' And רבי יוחנן said: This is flattery and arrogance that went down to בבל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question against the last line of the teaching. A פסוק, as explained by רבי יוחנן, says arrogance went to בבל, not to עילם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching gave arrogance to עילם. But רבי יוחנן reads the vision in זכריה as arrogance being carried to שנער, which is בבל. So the two sources seem to point to different places.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
The land of שנער, which is בבל

phrases.english: And did arrogance not go down to Babylonia?
But it is written: "I lifted my eyes and saw,
and behold, two women coming out,
with wind in their wings,
and they had wings like the wings of a stork,
and they lifted up the measure
between the earth and the heavens.
And I said to the angel who spoke with me:
Where are they taking the measure?

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלַי לִבְנוֹת לָהֿ בַיִת בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר״.
phrases.english: And he said to me: To build her a house in the land of Shinar."
phrases.notes: שנער is בבל. That is the whole point of the question.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is flattery and arrogance of spirit
that went down to Babylonia!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last line of Step 10, which gave arrogance to עילם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that עילם took nine portions of arrogance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק in זכריה as arrogance being brought to שנער (בבל). That contradicts placing arrogance in עילם.

steps.title: Arrogance came to בבל but slipped off to עילם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that arrogance did come down to בבל first, but it slipped away from there and settled in עילם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it came down to here (בבל), but it slipped off from here to there (עילם).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: both sources are true, because arrogance arrived in בבל but did not stay there. It moved on to עילם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes where arrogance was sent first. The teaching describes where it ended up. Once you separate 'arrived' from 'settled', the contradiction goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: To here (בבל, where the speakers lived)
Slipped away, made its way over

phrases.english: Yes, it came down to here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means בבל, where the חכמים of the גמרא lived.

phrases.english: but it slipped off and made its way over there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciliation: the two sources describe different stages, first arrival and then final settling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to say arrogance settled for good in בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Arrogance came to בבל first but moved on to עילם, so עילם holds the nine portions.

steps.title: The verse's wording supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the wording 'to build her a house' fits the answer. It only speaks of a plan to build a house in בבל, not a house that was actually built.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact, because it says 'to build her a house.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support for its answer from the exact words of the פסוק and concludes that the answer is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'to build her a house,' which describes a plan, not a finished home. That fits the idea that arrogance was meant to stay in בבל but did not actually settle there.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (it supports this reading)
Learn from it (conclude this is correct)

phrases.english: The wording is also exact,
since it says: "To build her a house,"
phrases.notes: It only says 'to build,' a plan, not that the house was actually built and lived in.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 12 from the wording of the פסוק quoted in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that arrogance came to בבל but did not stay there.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'לִבְנוֹת לָהּ בַּיִת' in זכריה, which describes a plan to build and not a finished house.

steps.title: Poverty is a sign of arrogance, and בבל is the poor place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a second challenge. A teaching says poverty is a sign of arrogance, and the poverty is in בבל, so arrogance should be in בבל too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But the Master said: a sign of arrogance is poverty. And poverty is found in בבל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer again. If poverty goes together with arrogance, and בבל has the poverty (Step 10), then בבל should have the arrogance too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge brings in a new source that ties arrogance to poverty. Step 10 itself gave nine portions of poverty to בבל, so the link points back to בבל and not to עילם.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't the Master say:
A sign of arrogance is poverty,
and it is in Babylonia that poverty is found!
phrases.notes: This goes back to Step 10, where בבל took nine portions of poverty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the conclusion that arrogance settled in עילם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that arrogance settled in עילם and not in בבל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Poverty is a sign of arrogance, and בבל holds the poverty. So arrogance should be found in בבל.

steps.title: The poverty meant is poverty in Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'poverty' that goes with arrogance is not money poverty but poverty in Torah, and that kind of poverty is found in עילם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What poverty is meant? Poverty in Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge by explaining which kind of poverty is the sign of arrogance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed 'poverty' meant lack of money, which is what בבל has. The answer redefines it as lack of Torah, so the sign of arrogance no longer points to בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Poverty in Torah, a lack of Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The word עניות means two different things here. In the 'ten portions' list it means money poverty (בבל). In 'a sign of arrogance is poverty' it means poverty in Torah (עילם).

phrases.english: What poverty is meant?
Poverty in Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: 'poverty' means lack of Torah, not lack of money.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The poverty that signals arrogance is money poverty, which is in בבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The poverty that signals arrogance is poverty in Torah, which is in עילם.

steps.title: עילם learned תורה but could not teach it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source showing that עילם is poor in Torah. On the פסוק 'We have a little sister, and she has no breasts,' רבי יוחנן says this is עילם, which merited to learn but not to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'We have a little sister, and she has no breasts.' And רבי יוחנן said: This is עילם, which merited to learn but did not merit to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that עילם has 'poverty in Torah' from a פסוק as explained by רבי יוחנן. This closes the discussion, and arrogance stays in עילם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sister with no breasts cannot nurse, meaning she cannot pass on what she has. עילם learned Torah but could not teach it to others, which is the 'poverty in Torah' that goes along with arrogance.
steps.whatToRemember: Arrogance came to בבל first but settled in עילם. The 'poverty' that is a sign of arrogance is poverty in Torah, and עילם learned Torah but could not teach it.

phrases.english: As it is written: "We have a little sister,
and she has no breasts,"
and Rabbi Yochanan said: This is Eilam,
which merited to learn,
but did not merit to teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״אָחוֹת לָנוּ קְטַנָּה וְשָׁדַיִם אֵין לָהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the answer of Step 15, that עילם is poor in Torah.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that עילם suffers from 'poverty in Torah.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים 8:8, explained by רבי יוחנן as referring to עילם, which learned but could not teach.

steps.title: The rest of the list of ten portions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the list of ten portions. For each trait, one group took nine portions and the rest of the world shared one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ten portions of strength came down to the world; פרס took nine. Lice: מדי took nine. Witchcraft: מצרים took nine. Plagues: pigs took nine. Immorality: ערביא took nine. Brazenness: מישן took nine. Talk: women took nine. Drunkenness: כושים took nine. Sleep: slaves took nine, and the whole rest of the world took one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list it started earlier and reads out the remaining items, one after another. It does not discuss them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא stopped only on arrogance (and the poverty linked to it) to ask questions. Wisdom, beauty and wealth were never questioned, and the remaining items raise no difficulty either, so they are simply listed. This closes the אגדה section before the new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of volume; here it just means a 'portion' of a trait
'And so on.' The rest of the line is left for the reader to fill in

steps.whatToRemember: The ten-portions list is now finished. Only some items needed questions; the rest are just listed, and the גמרא now moves to a new משנה.

phrases.english: Ten kav of strength came down to the world;
the Persians took nine, and so on.
Ten kav of lice came down to the world;
Media took nine, and so on.
Ten kav of witchcraft came down to the world;
Egypt took nine, and so on.
Ten kav of plagues came down to the world;
pigs took nine, and so on.
Ten kav of immorality came down to the world;
Arabia took nine, and so on.
Ten kav of brazenness came down to the world;
Meishan took nine, and so on.
Ten kav of talk came down to the world;
women took nine, and so on.
Ten kav of drunkenness came down to the world;
the Kushites took nine, and so on.
Ten kav of sleep came down to the world;
slaves took nine,
and the entire rest of the world took one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the questions about arrogance and poverty, the גמרא reads out the rest of the list with no further comment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each remaining trait came down in ten portions; one group took nine and the world shared one.

steps.title: False conditions about who he is and where he lives
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists cases where a man betroths a woman on a condition about his lineage, his city, or how close his house is to the bathhouse, and the truth turns out different.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'On condition that I am a כהן,' and he turned out to be a לוי, or the reverse; 'a נתין' and he turned out to be a ממזר, or the reverse; 'from a town' and he turned out to be from a city, or the reverse; 'on condition that my house is near the bathhouse' and it turned out far, or the reverse.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a list of cases where a man gives קידושין based on a claim about himself that turns out false. The ruling for these cases comes at the end of the list, in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case comes in pairs that go both ways: once he is 'better' than he claimed and once 'worse.' This pairing teaches that the condition counts as written. The woman may have had her own reasons to want exactly what he described.

keyTerms.meaning: And it turned out (that he was)
A descendant of the Gibeonites, forbidden to marry into the community
Someone from a small town / someone from a big city

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think she is betrothed when he turns out 'better' than he said (a כהן instead of a לוי, or a house close to the bathhouse instead of far). The משנה deliberately gives both directions, and in every case the condition was not met.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he said, 'Be betrothed to me on the condition that I am a priest,'
and he turned out to be a Levite;
or 'a Levite,' and he turned out to be a priest;
or 'a Gibeonite,' and he turned out to be a mamzer;
or 'a mamzer,' and he turned out to be a Gibeonite;
or 'a resident of a town,' and he turned out to be a resident of a city;
or 'a resident of a city,' and he turned out to be a resident of a town;
or 'on the condition that my house is close to the bathhouse,'
and it turned out to be far;
or 'far,' and it turned out to be close.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֲנִי כֹּהֵן וְנִמְצָא לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the אגדה section is over, and a new משנה about conditional קידושין begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cases of קידושין based on a false claim about his lineage, city, or home location. The ruling (not betrothed) comes in step 20.

steps.title: False conditions about his daughter, maidservant, or sons
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues the list with conditions about whether he has a grown daughter or maidservant, or sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if he said, 'On condition that he has a grown daughter or maidservant,' and he does not, or 'that he does not,' and he does. Or 'on condition that he has no sons,' and he does, or 'that he has sons,' and he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds more cases of the same kind, this time about the man's household. The ruling for all the cases is still coming in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again every case goes both ways. Whether having a daughter, a maidservant, or sons is good or bad for her, what counts is that his claim was false.

keyTerms.meaning: He has / he does not have

phrases.english: Or 'on the condition that he has a daughter'
phrases.notes: The משנה describes the man's own claim about himself, just in third person ('he').

phrases.english: or a grown maidservant,' and he does not have one;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ״ וְיֵשׁ לוֹ.
phrases.english: or 'on the condition that he does not have one,' and he does;

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּנִים״ וְיֵשׁ לוֹ,
phrases.english: or 'on the condition that he has no sons,' and he does;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַל מְנָת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ וְאֵין לוֹ.
phrases.english: or on the condition that he has sons, and he does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מְנָת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בַּת אוֹ שִׁפְחָה מְגוּדֶּלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of false conditions, moving from his status and home to his household.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: More cases of false conditions, about his daughter, maidservant, or sons.

steps.title: Ruling: she is not betrothed, even if she says she didn't care
steps.stepSummary: In all the cases listed, she is not betrothed, even if she later says she meant to marry him anyway. The same applies if she was the one who made a false claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: In all of these cases, even though she said, 'In my heart I meant to be betrothed to him anyway,' she is still not betrothed. The same is true if she was the one who misled him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the ruling for every case in steps 18 and 19: the קידושין does not take effect. It adds that the rule works the same way when the woman made the false condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition spoken out loud decides the matter. Her private thoughts afterward ('I would have accepted him anyway') cannot override it. The last line flips the cases: if she betrothed herself on a false claim about herself, the קידושין also fails.

keyTerms.meaning: In my heart, privately in my mind

steps.whatToRemember: When קידושין is given on a spoken condition that turns out false, she is not betrothed. This holds whether the truth is better or worse than the claim, despite her later claim that she didn't care, and whether he or she made the false claim.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a spoken condition outweighs unspoken thoughts. It is a key idea for conditional קידושין and for the discussion that follows.

phrases.english: And in all of them, even though she said:
'In my heart I meant to be betrothed to him,'

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: even so, she is not betrothed.
And the same is true if it was she who misled him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְכוּלָּם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרָה בְּלִבִּי הָיָה לְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for all the cases listed in steps 18 and 19 and extends it to a woman who misleads.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In every case of a false condition she is not betrothed, even if she claims she didn't care, and the same applies when she made the false claim.

steps.title: A man sells his property, planning to move to ארץ ישראל, and רבא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: A man sold his property because he planned to move to ארץ ישראל but said nothing about it at the sale. רבא rules that thoughts kept in the heart have no legal weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man sold his property because he intended to go up to ארץ ישראל, but when he sold it he said nothing about that. רבא said: this is a matter kept in the heart, and matters kept in the heart do not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case about a sale made for an unspoken reason, and רבא gives a ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller had a clear private reason for selling, but he never made it a stated condition. רבא rules that a reason you never say out loud cannot cancel a deal, so the sale stays valid even if the plan falls through.

keyTerms.meaning: With the intention of; with this in mind
Matters in the heart: private intentions never said out loud

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: דברים שבלב אינם דברים. An unspoken intention cannot undo a deal.
steps.confusionAlert: The man really did have this intention. רבא is not doubting that. He is saying that an intention you never stated has no legal effect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule has major practical weight for sales and agreements: only stated conditions can undo a deal, not private thoughts.

phrases.english: GEMARA
A certain man who sold his property
with the intention of going up to Eretz Yisrael,
and at the time that he sold
he did not say anything.
phrases.notes: The גמרא takes the rest of the story for granted: in the end he didn't go, and he wanted to cancel the sale.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is a matter in the heart,
and matters in the heart are not matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה about conditions in קידושין by bringing a case about an unstated condition in a sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intention never stated at the time of sale (דברים שבלב) does not affect the sale.

steps.title: Where does רבא learn this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבא's source and begins to suggest one from a taught source.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רבא learn this? If we say it comes from what was taught:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source רבא's rule is based on. It then starts to offer a possible source, which is quoted at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אילימא ("if we say") usually signals that the first suggested source will be questioned or rejected. So this line sets up the next move rather than giving a final answer.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?
If we say: introduces a suggestion that is often later rejected
We learned: introduces a taught source

phrases.english: From where does Rava get this?
If we say it is from that which we learned:
phrases.notes: The source itself is quoted at the start of the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רבא's ruling in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבא's principle that דברים שבלב אינם דברים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A first source is about to be proposed, introduced by אילימא.
